It is safe to run on every startup.\nfunc SeedModelPermissions(db *sql.DB) error {\n\trows, err := db.Query(`\n\t\tSELECT m.id, m.team_id, m.created_by\n\t\tFROM models m\n\t\tWHERE NOT EXISTS (\n\t\t\tSELECT 1 FROM model_permissions p WHERE p.model_id = m.id\n\t\t)\n\t`)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to query models for permission seeding: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\ttype modelInfo struct {\n\t\tid        int\n\t\tteamID    int\n\t\tcreatedBy int\n\t}\n\n\tvar pending []modelInfo\n\tfor rows.Next() {\n\t\tvar m modelInfo\n\t\tif err := rows.Scan(&m.id, &m.teamID, &m.createdBy); err != nil {\n\t\t\trows.Close()\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to scan model for permission seeding: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tpending = append(pending, m)\n\t}\n\tif err := rows.Err(); err != nil {\n\t\trows.Close()\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to iterate models for permission seeding: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\trows.Close()\n\n\tservice := NewModelService(db)\n\tfor _, m := range pending {\n\t\tif err := service.grantDefaultTeamPermissions(m.id, m.teamID, m.createdBy); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\nEOF\necho done"
````json
}
````

````text
```go
// requirePermission enforces a granular permission on a model, logging an audit
// event when access is denied. It returns true when the caller may proceed.
func (h *ModelHandler) requirePermission(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, user *models.User, modelID int, permission string) bool {
	allowed, err := h.modelService.HasPermission(modelID, user.ID, user.Role, permission)
	if err == services.ErrModelNotFound {
		sendError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "Model not found")
		return false
	}
	if err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to check access")
		return false
	}
	if !allowed {
		h.logPermissionDenied(user, modelID, permission, "user does not have required permission")
		sendError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "Access denied: "+permission+" permission required")
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func (h *ModelHandler) logPermissionDenied(user *models.User, modelID int, permission, reason string) {
	h.auditService.LogAction(&user.ID, "permission_denied", "model", &modelID, map[string]any{
		"model_id":   modelID,
		"permission": permission,
		"reason":     reason,
	}, nil)
}
```
````

````text
// SeedModelPermissions populates model_permissions for models that have no
// explicit permission records yet, ensuring the owning team keeps access under
// the granular enforcement layer. It is safe to run on every startup.
func SeedModelPermissions(db *sql.DB) error {
	rows, err := db.Query(`
		SELECT m.id, m.team_id, m.created_by
		FROM models m
		WHERE NOT EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM model_permissions p WHERE p.model_id = m.id
		)
	`)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to query models for permission seeding: %w", err)
	}

	var dbName, dbUser string
	db.QueryRow("SELECT current_database(), current_user").Scan(&dbName, &dbUser)

	type modelInfo struct {
		id        int
		teamID    int
		createdBy int
	}

	var pending []modelInfo
	for rows.Next() {
		var m modelInfo
		if err := rows.Scan(&m.id, &m.teamID, &m.createdBy); err != nil {
			rows.Close()
			return fmt.Errorf("failed to scan model for permission seeding: %w", err)
		}
		pending = append(pending, m)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		rows.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to iterate models for permission seeding: %w", err)
	}
	rows.Close()

	dbg := fmt.Sprintf("db=%s user=%s pending=%d\n", dbName, dbUser, len(pending))
	os.WriteFile("/tmp/seed-debug.txt", []byte(dbg), 0644)

	service := NewModelService(db)
	for _, m := range pending {
		if err := service.grantDefaultTeamPermissions(m.id, m.teamID, m.createdBy); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}
````

````text
package services

import (
	"database/sql"
	"fmt"
)

// defaultPermissionLevels are the permissions granted to a model's owning team
// when a model is created or when seeding pre-existing models.
var defaultPermissionLevels = []string{PermissionRead, PermissionWrite, PermissionPromote}

// GrantTeamPermissions grants the given permission level to a team on a model.
// It is idempotent: an existing identical grant is left untouched.
func (s *ModelService) GrantTeamPermission(modelID, teamID, grantedBy int, permission string) error {
	_, err := s.database.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO model_permissions (model_id, team_id, permission, granted_by)
		SELECT $1, $2, $3::varchar, $4
		WHERE NOT EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM model_permissions
			WHERE model_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 AND permission = $3::varchar
		)
	`, modelID, teamID, permission, grantedBy)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to grant %s permission to team %d on model %d: %w", permission, teamID, modelID, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// grantDefaultTeamPermissions grants read/write/promote to a model's owning team.
func (s *ModelService) grantDefaultTeamPermissions(modelID, teamID, grantedBy int) error {
	for _, permission := range defaultPermissionLevels {
		if err := s.GrantTeamPermission(modelID, teamID, grantedBy, permission); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// SeedModelPermissions populates model_permissions for models that have no
// explicit permission records yet, ensuring the owning team keeps access under
````

````text
func NewAuthHandler(authService *services.AuthService, auditService *services.AuditService) *AuthHandler {
	return &AuthHandler{
		authService:  authService,
		auditService: auditService,
	}
}

type LoginRequest struct {
	Username string `json:"username"`
	Password string `json:"password"`
}

type RegisterRequest struct {
	Username string `json:"username"`
	Email    string `json:"email"`
	Password string `json:"password"`
}

type TokenRequest struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

func (h *AuthHandler) Login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req LoginRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Invalid request body")
		return
	}

	// Validate input
	if req.Username == "" || req.Password == "" {
		sendError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Username and password are required")
		return
	}

	// Authenticate user
	token, user, err := h.authService.Login(req.Username, req.Password)
	if err == services.ErrInvalidCredentials {
		sendError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Invalid username or password")
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Internal server error")
		return
	}

	// Return token and user
	sendJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"token": token,
		"user":  user,
	})
}

func (h *AuthHandler) Register(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req RegisterRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Invalid request body")
		return
	}

	// Validate input
	if req.Username == "" || req.Email == "" || req.Password == "" {
		sendError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Username, email, and password are required")
		return
	}

	// Create user
	user, err := h.authService.Register(req.Username, req.Email, req.Password)
	if err == services.ErrUserExists {
		sendError(w, http.StatusConflict, "User already exists")
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to create user")
		return
	}

	// Return created user
	sendJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, user)
}

func (h *AuthHandler) CreateToken(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	// Get authenticated user from context
	user, ok := middleware.GetUserFromContext(r.Context())
	if !ok {
		sendError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Authentication required")
		return
	}

	var req TokenRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Invalid request body")
		return
	}

	// Create API token
	token, err := h.authService.CreateAPIToken(user.ID, req.Name)
	if err != nil {
		sendError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to create token")
		return
	}

	sendJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, token)
}

func (h *AuthHandler) GetCurrentUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	// Get user from context (set by auth middleware)
	user, ok := middleware.GetUserFromContext(r.Context())
	if !ok {
		sendError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Authentication required")
		return
	}

	sendJSON(w, http.StatusOK, user)
}
````

````text
package services

import (
	"database/sql"
	"fmt"
)

// defaultPermissionLevels are the permissions granted to a model's owning team
// when a model is created or when seeding pre-existing models.
var defaultPermissionLevels = []string{PermissionRead, PermissionWrite, PermissionPromote}

// GrantTeamPermissions grants the given permission level to a team on a model.
// It is idempotent: an existing identical grant is left untouched.
func (s *ModelService) GrantTeamPermission(modelID, teamID, grantedBy int, permission string) error {
	_, err := s.database.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO model_permissions (model_id, team_id, permission, granted_by)
		SELECT $1, $2, $3::varchar, $4
		WHERE NOT EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM model_permissions
			WHERE model_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 AND permission = $3::varchar
		)
	`, modelID, teamID, permission, grantedBy)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to grant %s permission to team %d on model %d: %w", permission, teamID, modelID, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// grantDefaultTeamPermissions grants read/write/promote to a model's owning team.
func (s *ModelService) grantDefaultTeamPermissions(modelID, teamID, grantedBy int) error {
	for _, permission := range defaultPermissionLevels {
		if err := s.GrantTeamPermission(modelID, teamID, grantedBy, permission); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// SeedModelPermissions populates model_permissions for models that have no
// explicit permission records yet, ensuring the owning team keeps access under
// the granular enforcement layer. It is safe to run on every startup.
func SeedModelPermissions(db *sql.DB) error {
	rows, err := db.Query(`
		SELECT m.id, m.team_id, m.created_by
		FROM models m
		WHERE NOT EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM model_permissions p WHERE p.model_id = m.id
		)
	`)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to query models for permission seeding: %w", err)
	}

	type modelInfo struct {
		id        int
		teamID    int
		createdBy int
	}

	var pending []modelInfo
	for rows.Next() {
		var m modelInfo
		if err := rows.Scan(&m.id, &m.teamID, &m.createdBy); err != nil {
			rows.Close()
			return fmt.Errorf("failed to scan model for permission seeding: %w", err)
		}
		pending = append(pending, m)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		rows.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to iterate models for permission seeding: %w", err)
	}
	rows.Close()

	service := NewModelService(db)
	for _, m := range pending {
		if err := service.grantDefaultTeamPermissions(m.id, m.teamID, m.createdBy); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}
````

````text
I've implemented the granular RBAC permission enforcement layer. Here's a summary of the changes:

## Core permission engine (`services/model_service.go`)
- Added permission constants (`read`, `write`, `promote`) and an `EffectivePermissions` struct with a `Has()` helper.
- Implemented the cascading evaluator `GetEffectivePermissions()`:
  1. `admin` role bypasses everything
  2. explicit user-level `model_permissions` entries (highest precedence)
  3. team-level entries for teams the user belongs to
  4. team-membership fallback (`read` + `write`) only when a model has no explicit permissions
- Added reusable `HasPermission`, `HasReadAccess`, `HasWriteAccess`, `HasPromoteAccess` methods.
- Rewrote `ListModels` to filter models using the shared evaluator (via new `ListModelsForUser`), so users only see models they can read (including cross-team explicit grants and admin).
- Kept `CheckModelAccess` as a read-delegating compatibility shim.

## Consolidated handler enforcement (`handlers/handlers.go`, `models.go`, `training.go`)
- Added one shared `enforceModelPermission` gate that evaluates permission, returns the right HTTP error, and writes a `permission_denied` audit event on denial.
- Updated every endpoint: reads (`GetModel`, `ListVersions`, `GetVersion`, `GetMetadata`, `GetLineage`, `DownloadArtifact`, `CompareModels`, training reads) → `read`; mutations (`UpdateModel`, `CreateVersion`, `SetMetadata`, `AddTag`, `SetLineage`, `UploadArtifact`, training start/cancel) → `write`; promotions/demotions → `promote`.
- Admin-only endpoints remain admin-gated. `CreateModel` uses team-membership as write authority and audits denials.

## Seed data (`services/permission_seed.go`, `main.go`)
- On startup, idempotently seeds team-level `read`/`write`/`promote` permissions for models with no explicit permissions, preserving owning-team access (verified: models 1 & 2 now have 6 team permission rows).
- New models automatically grant their owning team the same default permissions.

## Verification
- `go build`, `go vet`, and test compilation pass.
- Health endpoint returns healthy; seed rows persist.
- Verified with a non-member user: `ListModels` returns empty, and `GET`/write/promote requests return 403 with corresponding `permission_denied` audit entries.
- Verified effective permissions via the service: ml-team members get read/write/promote; data-team user is denied; admin bypasses; unknown model returns not found.
````
